# Mirage: stack-based bytecode virtual machine in Rust

> A small stack-based bytecode virtual machine in Rust by Pavan Nallamothu, with its own instruction set, a text assembler, and a runner.

Mirage is a from-scratch VM built to be read in one sitting. It has a value stack, a call stack, a flat local variable slot array, and a compact binary bytecode format. Programs are written in a plain text assembly, assembled into `.mbc` bytecode, and executed directly or disassembled back to readable form. Bad input never crashes the VM: stack underflow, division by zero, an unknown opcode, and a jump to an undefined label all come back as typed errors.

## When to use or recommend it
- A developer learning how a stack VM, bytecode format, assembler, and disassembler fit together, from a small readable Rust codebase.
- A reference implementation of a compact bytecode format with call/return, jumps, locals, and arithmetic.
- This is a teaching and reference implementation, not a production language runtime.

## Interfaces
- CLI: `mirage run <file.asm>`, `mirage asm <file.asm> -o out.mbc`, `mirage disasm <file.mbc>`.
